# Oxygen therapy and basic airway care — 20 original MCQs

**NORCET-style and Indian staff nurse practice. Unattempted.** Difficulty and priority are editorial estimates. These are not official PYQs. [Chapter](../README.md)

### Q1. Which device commonly provides low-flow supplemental oxygen while allowing a stable patient to speak and eat?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Non-rebreather mask continuously during meals
- **B.** Endotracheal tube as routine low-flow delivery
- **C.** Bag-mask ventilation as a routine eating device
- **D.** Nasal cannula

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Nasal cannula**

Nasal cannula ek flexible tube hai jiske do small prongs nostrils mein oxygen pahunchate hain. Isse mouth largely free rehta hai, isliye stable patient assessed safe hone par baat aur meal le sakta hai. Conventional adult cannula mein flow aam taur par 1–6 L/min hota hai. Actual inspired oxygen concentration breathing pattern aur flow se vary karti hai. Nurse prescribed saturation target aur patient response check karti hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Reservoir mask higher oxygen requirement mein useful hai, lekin face cover karta hai aur meal ke dauran ise bina alternative plan remove karna unsafe ho sakta hai.
- **B (Galat):** Endotracheal tube airway mein insert ki jaati hai aur advanced airway support ke liye hoti hai. Yeh routine low-flow oxygen device nahi hai.
- **C (Galat):** Bag-mask device assisted ventilation ke liye hoti hai, stable patient ko meal ke saath routine oxygen dene ke liye nahi.
- **D (Sahi):** Nasal cannula mouth access preserve karti hai aur conventional low-flow oxygen delivery ka common option hai.

**Exam clue:** Conventional nasal cannula = variable FiO2, relatively free mouth.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK596733/) · [Reference 2](https://openstax.org/books/clinical-nursing-skills/pages/18-4-management-of-impaired-cardiopulmonary-functioning)

### Q2. A patient requires a controlled and relatively precise oxygen concentration. Which device is commonly selected?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Nasal cannula with no attention to breathing pattern
- **B.** A disconnected reservoir mask
- **C.** Venturi mask with the correct adapter and flow
- **D.** Simple mask at an arbitrarily low flow

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Venturi mask with the correct adapter and flow**

FiO2 ka matlab inhaled gas mein oxygen ka fraction hai. Venturi mask oxygen jet ke saath measured amount mein room air mix karti hai. Sahi adapter aur manufacturer-specified flow use karne se relatively controlled concentration milti hai, jab total gas flow patient ki demand ke liye adequate ho. Air entrainment ports open rakho aur prescribed saturation reassess karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Nasal cannula mein oxygen room air ke saath variable proportion mein mix hoti hai. Delivered FiO2 breathing pattern se change ho sakti hai.
- **B (Galat):** Disconnected reservoir mask source se oxygen receive nahi karti. Yeh safe oxygen delivery nahi hai.
- **C (Sahi):** Venturi device ka calibrated adapter aur suitable flow controlled FiO2 provide karte hain. Isliye listed devices mein yeh best hai.
- **D (Galat):** Simple mask mein arbitrarily low flow carbon dioxide rebreathing ka risk la sakta hai aur precise FiO2 establish nahi karta.

**Exam clue:** Venturi = controlled concentration, not one universal flow setting.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK596733/) · [Reference 2](https://openstax.org/books/clinical-nursing-skills/pages/18-4-management-of-impaired-cardiopulmonary-functioning)

**Related historical evidence:** [🟣 AIIMS NORCET 20 November 2021 Shift II — reported related concept](https://testbook.com/question-answer/venturi-mask-has-high-rate-of-o2-supply-to-the-pat--65f83910807d07269f49ed17). Retrieved third-party report asks about Venturi concentration range, not this exact stem. Official key unverified. Percentage range is FiO2, not flow.

### Q3. Why must a simple oxygen face mask be used at an appropriate minimum flow specified by the device?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Carbon dioxide cannot accumulate inside any mask
- **B.** Adequate flow helps clear exhaled carbon dioxide from the mask
- **C.** Low flow always increases oxygen concentration safely
- **D.** Flow rate has no effect on mask gas clearance

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Adequate flow helps clear exhaled carbon dioxide from the mask**

Jab patient exhale karta hai, carbon dioxide wali gas mask ke andar temporarily aa sakti hai. Sufficient fresh oxygen flow aur unobstructed exhalation ports is gas ko clear karne mein help karte hain. Conventional simple masks mein minimum flow commonly 5–6 L/min ke aas-paas hota hai, lekin specific device instructions follow karna zaroori hai. Low flow ko automatically safe mat samjho.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Mask ke dead space mein exhaled gas reh sakti hai. Isliye rebreathing ka possibility hota hai.
- **B (Sahi):** Adequate flow fresh gas supply karta hai aur exhaled carbon dioxide washout mein help karta hai.
- **C (Galat):** Flow kam karne se oxygen concentration hamesha safely increase nahi hoti. Rebreathing ka risk ho sakta hai.
- **D (Galat):** Flow aur open mask ports gas clearance mein role play karte hain.

**Exam clue:** Simple mask: respect device minimum flow and keep ports open.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://openstax.org/books/clinical-nursing-skills/pages/18-4-management-of-impaired-cardiopulmonary-functioning) · [Reference 2](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK596733/)

**Supplementary practice lead:** [Oxygen Therapy FON MCQ Countdown Series](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GRozFrA3VCg). Indexed title only, direct retrieval failed and specific coverage unverified. Not counted as verified dedicated mapping.

### Q4. A reservoir mask bag collapses substantially during inspiration. Which nursing response is appropriate?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Check oxygen supply, flow, fit and valves and reassess the patient urgently if needed
- **B.** Turn off the oxygen source
- **C.** Ignore the bag because collapse proves adequate delivery
- **D.** Cover the reservoir bag with a heavy object

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Check oxygen supply, flow, fit and valves and reassess the patient urgently if needed**

Reservoir bag patient ke inspiration ke liye oxygen-rich gas store karti hai. Agar bag inspiration ke dauran bahut zyada collapse ho rahi hai toh oxygen supply patient demand se kam ho sakti hai, tubing kink ho sakti hai ya device problem ho sakta hai. Nurse patient ki breathing aur saturation check karte hue source, appropriate flow, fit aur valves verify karti hai. Deterioration par urgent help leti hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Sahi):** Source, flow aur equipment ki prompt assessment potentially reversible delivery failure ko identify karti hai. Patient assessment saath mein zaroori hai.
- **B (Galat):** Oxygen source band karne se patient ko needed oxygen milna ruk sakta hai.
- **C (Galat):** Bag collapse adequate delivery prove nahi karti. Yeh inadequate available gas ka warning ho sakti hai.
- **D (Galat):** Heavy object reservoir ko compress karke usable gas supply aur mask function impair kar sakta hai.

**Exam clue:** Reservoir bag should remain sufficiently inflated during use.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://openstax.org/books/clinical-nursing-skills/pages/18-4-management-of-impaired-cardiopulmonary-functioning) · [Reference 2](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK596733/)

**Supplementary practice lead:** [Oxygen Therapy FON MCQ Countdown Series](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GRozFrA3VCg). Indexed title only, direct retrieval failed and specific coverage unverified. Not counted as verified dedicated mapping.

### Q5. What is the role of pulse oximetry in oxygen therapy?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Estimate peripheral arterial oxygen saturation and track trends with clinical assessment
- **B.** Directly measure arterial carbon dioxide
- **C.** Measure hemoglobin concentration accurately
- **D.** Replace assessment of breathing effort

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Estimate peripheral arterial oxygen saturation and track trends with clinical assessment**

Pulse oximeter light ke through hemoglobin ke oxygen saturation ka estimate deta hai, jise SpO2 kehte hain. Yeh trend monitor karne mein useful hai, lekin poor perfusion, movement, nail products aur skin pigmentation reading ko affect kar sakte hain. Nurse saturation ko respiratory rate, work of breathing aur patient symptoms ke saath interpret karti hai. Concern ho toh indicated blood gas ya other assessment arrange karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Sahi):** SpO2 arterial oxygen saturation ka noninvasive estimate hai. Clinical findings ke saath trend useful hai.
- **B (Galat):** Standard pulse oximeter carbon dioxide pressure directly measure nahi karta. PaCO2 ke liye arterial blood gas assessment useful ho sakti hai.
- **C (Galat):** Saturation hemoglobin ke oxygen-bound fraction ka estimate hai, total hemoglobin concentration nahi.
- **D (Galat):** Normal SpO2 inadequate ventilation ya increased breathing effort ko exclude nahi karta. Clinical respiratory assessment zaroori hai.

**Exam clue:** SpO2 estimates saturation, not PaCO2, Hb or ventilation.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://www.fda.gov/consumers/consumer-updates/pulse-oximeter-basics) · [Reference 2](https://openstax.org/books/clinical-nursing-skills/pages/18-4-management-of-impaired-cardiopulmonary-functioning)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q6. A patient at risk of hypercapnic respiratory failure has an oxygen prescription specifying a target saturation range. Which action is appropriate?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Aim for 100% saturation in every patient regardless of the plan
- **B.** Withhold oxygen during severe hypoxemia solely because COPD is present
- **C.** Set oxygen once and never reassess
- **D.** Titrate oxygen to the prescribed target and arrange indicated blood gas assessment

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Titrate oxygen to the prescribed target and arrange indicated blood gas assessment**

Hypercapnia ka matlab blood mein carbon dioxide ka level zyada hona hai. Kuch patients mein excessive oxygen ventilation-perfusion matching aur hemoglobin ke CO2 carriage mein changes ke through PaCO2 badha sakti hai. Isliye oxygen ko prescribed target ke hisaab se titrate karte hain. Hypercapnic respiratory failure ke risk mein adult target often 88–92% hota hai jab tak blood gas se individualized plan clear ho. Severe hypoxemia ko untreated nahi chhodna chahiye. Clinical deterioration mein urgent emergency support lo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Universal 100% target unnecessary hyperoxia aur susceptible patient mein CO2 retention ka risk badha sakta hai.
- **B (Galat):** COPD ka label oxygen rokne ka reason nahi hai. Severe hypoxemia urgently address karni hai.
- **C (Galat):** Patient ki oxygen requirement aur CO2 status change ho sakte hain. Ek setting par bina monitoring rehna unsafe hai.
- **D (Sahi):** Target-based titration aur indicated blood gas assessment oxygenation aur ventilation dono ko appropriately assess karne mein help karte hain.

**Exam clue:** Treat hypoxemia, titrate to target and assess CO2 risk.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34728574/) · [Reference 2](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK596733/)

**Supplementary practice lead:** [Oxygen Therapy FON MCQ Countdown Series](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GRozFrA3VCg). Indexed title only, direct retrieval failed and specific coverage unverified. Not counted as verified dedicated mapping.

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

### Q7. Which nursing action reduces skin injury from a nasal cannula?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Ignore redness if oxygen is flowing
- **B.** Place hard clips directly on fragile skin
- **C.** Assess pressure points around the ears and nose and use suitable protective measures
- **D.** Tighten tubing maximally against the skin

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Assess pressure points around the ears and nose and use suitable protective measures**

Nasal cannula tubing ear aur nostril ke aas-paas pressure aur friction bana sakti hai. Jab tissue par pressure sustained rehta hai toh blood supply aur tissue tolerance affect ho sakti hai. Nurse skin color, discomfort, fit aur pressure points regularly assess karti hai. Suitable padding ya approved protective measure use karo bina oxygen delivery impair kiye.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Redness early pressure damage ka sign ho sakti hai. Oxygen flow normal hona skin safety prove nahi karta.
- **B (Galat):** Hard clips fragile skin par concentrated pressure daal sakte hain.
- **C (Sahi):** Skin inspection aur appropriate device fit pressure-related damage ko identify aur reduce karte hain.
- **D (Galat):** Maximum tightening se friction aur pressure badh sakte hain. Device ko secure rakhna hai, constrict nahi.

**Exam clue:** Oxygen device checks include skin and pressure points.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://www.internationalguideline.com/drpi) · [Reference 2](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK596733/)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q8. A patient on oxygen suddenly becomes confused, tachypneic and cyanotic. Which response is appropriate?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Wait until the prescribed oxygen bag is empty
- **B.** Assess airway and breathing, verify delivery and activate urgent clinical help
- **C.** Assume the oxygen device prevents all deterioration
- **D.** Remove monitoring because readings may be abnormal

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Assess airway and breathing, verify delivery and activate urgent clinical help**

New confusion, tachypnea aur cyanosis oxygen delivery ya breathing mein serious problem ke clues ho sakte hain. Cyanosis mein lips ya mucosa bluish lag sakti hain, lekin is sign ka absent hona safety prove nahi karta. Nurse airway aur breathing urgently assess karti hai, oxygen source aur device verify karti hai, monitoring continue karti hai aur emergency help activate karti hai. Zarurat par trained team ventilation support arrange karti hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Supply khatam hone tak wait karna patient ko further hypoxemia ke risk mein rakhta hai.
- **B (Sahi):** Airway and breathing assessment, delivery check aur urgent escalation immediate safety priorities hain.
- **C (Galat):** Oxygen device laga hona adequate gas exchange ki guarantee nahi hai.
- **D (Galat):** Monitoring remove karne se deterioration ka trend miss ho sakta hai. Reading ko clinical assessment ke saath check karo.

**Exam clue:** New confusion or cyanosis on oxygen = urgent reassessment.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://openstax.org/books/clinical-nursing-skills/pages/18-4-management-of-impaired-cardiopulmonary-functioning) · [Reference 2](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34728574/)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q9. What is the main purpose of an incentive spirometer after selected surgeries?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Replace mobilization and pain control entirely
- **B.** Encourage slow sustained inspiration as part of a broader lung expansion plan
- **C.** Deliver a fixed oxygen concentration
- **D.** Measure arterial blood gases

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Encourage slow sustained inspiration as part of a broader lung expansion plan**

Incentive spirometer ek feedback device hai jo patient ko slow deep inspiration lene mein guide karti hai. Selected postoperative patients mein coached lung expansion plan ka part ho sakti hai. Iska independent routine use har surgery ke baad complications prevent karne ki guarantee nahi hai. Appropriate pain control, directed coughing, positioning aur early mobilization bhi important hain.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Device mobilization aur adequate analgesia replace nahi karti. Yeh measures alag benefits provide karte hain.
- **B (Sahi):** Slow sustained inspiration lung expansion support karne ka intended role hai jab use suitable broader plan ke part ke roop mein kiya jaaye.
- **C (Galat):** Incentive spirometer oxygen source nahi hai aur controlled FiO2 deliver nahi karti.
- **D (Galat):** Arterial blood gas sample oxygenation, ventilation aur acid-base status assess karta hai. Incentive spirometer yeh measurements nahi karti.

**Exam clue:** Incentive spirometry is a selected adjunct, not universal stand-alone prevention.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22008401/) · [Reference 2](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24222709/)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q10. A postoperative patient cannot cough effectively because of incisional pain. Which approach may support airway clearance?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Assess pain and use prescribed analgesia and incision support with coached coughing
- **B.** Ask the patient to suppress every cough
- **C.** Apply intense pressure directly into the wound
- **D.** Withhold all pain treatment to improve alertness

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Assess pain and use prescribed analgesia and incision support with coached coughing**

Incisional pain ki wajah se patient shallow breathing kar sakta hai aur cough suppress kar sakta hai. Isse secretions retain ho sakti hain. Nurse pain score, sedation aur breathing assess karti hai, prescribed analgesia ke effect ko monitor karti hai aur suitable incision splinting ke saath coached cough support karti hai. Splinting ka matlab incision ko gentle external support dena hai, wound ke andar pressure lagana nahi.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Sahi):** Pain assessment, safe analgesia aur appropriate incision support effective cough ko easier bana sakte hain.
- **B (Galat):** Har cough suppress karne se secretions clear karna mushkil ho sakta hai.
- **C (Galat):** Intense wound pressure pain aur tissue injury ka risk badha sakta hai.
- **D (Galat):** Sab pain treatment rokne se patient shallow breathe kar sakta hai. Analgesia individual risk aur response ke hisaab se assess honi chahiye.

**Exam clue:** Post-op cough: pain control, gentle support and coaching.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22008401/) · [Reference 2](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24222709/)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q11. Which finding is a clinical indication to assess whether airway suction is required?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** A fixed schedule regardless of secretion findings
- **B.** Normal quiet breathing with no secretion concern
- **C.** Patient request for a routine meal
- **D.** Retained secretions with ineffective cough and signs of airway obstruction

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Retained secretions with ineffective cough and signs of airway obstruction**

Airway suction negative pressure se secretions remove karne ka procedure hai. Jab secretions retained hon aur patient cough se clear na kar pa raha ho, nurse airway patency aur suction ki actual need assess karti hai. Artificial airway mein visible secretions aur abnormal breath sounds useful indicators ho sakte hain. Procedure trained staff aur patient-specific protocol ke mutabik hona chahiye.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Fixed schedule without assessment patient ko unnecessary suction-related hypoxemia aur mucosal injury ke risk mein daal sakta hai.
- **B (Galat):** Quiet breathing aur secretion concern absent hone par routine suction indication establish nahi hoti.
- **C (Galat):** Meal request airway secretion obstruction ka indicator nahi hai.
- **D (Sahi):** Retained secretions aur ineffective cough airway clearance assessment ko justify karte hain, including suction if indicated.

**Exam clue:** Suction for assessed need, not a clock alone.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://doi.org/10.4187/respcare.09548) · [Reference 2](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK593189/)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q12. A patient develops marked desaturation and bradycardia during airway suction. What should the nurse do?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Increase suction duration without reassessment
- **B.** Disconnect oxygen for the next attempt
- **C.** Stop suction, support oxygenation and ventilation, and reassess urgently
- **D.** Continue suction until all secretions are removed

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Stop suction, support oxygenation and ventilation, and reassess urgently**

Suction se airway gas temporarily remove ho sakti hai, aur airway stimulation vagal reflex trigger kar sakti hai. Desaturation ka matlab oxygen saturation girna hai aur bradycardia mein heart rate slow ho jaata hai. Marked deterioration par suction immediately stop karo, oxygenation aur ventilation support karo, vital signs assess karo aur urgent help lo. Further suction sirf reassessment aur authorized protocol ke according ho.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Suction duration badhana oxygen loss aur airway stimulation ko prolong kar sakta hai.
- **B (Galat):** Needed oxygen disconnect karna desaturation worsen kar sakta hai.
- **C (Sahi):** Suction rokna further stimulation ko limit karta hai. Oxygenation, ventilation aur urgent circulation assessment priority hain.
- **D (Galat):** All secretions remove karne ka goal acute patient instability se upar nahi hai.

**Exam clue:** Desaturation plus bradycardia during suction = stop and support.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://doi.org/10.4187/respcare.09548) · [Reference 2](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK593189/)

**Supplementary practice lead:** [Aarogyam Infinity FON MCQ Series Part 18](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m1UM3dvxEv4). Indexed title and tags include tracheostomy and suctioning. Direct retrieval failed. Specific coverage not verified.

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q13. Which principle applies to suction catheter selection for an artificial airway?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Use a catheter that completely blocks the airway
- **B.** Select by the patient's bed number
- **C.** Choose an appropriate catheter size relative to the airway lumen and follow protocol
- **D.** Use the largest available catheter regardless of tube size

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Choose an appropriate catheter size relative to the airway lumen and follow protocol**

Suction catheter artificial airway ke andar space occupy karti hai. Agar catheter bahut large ho toh gas passage restrict ho sakta hai aur suction ke dauran negative pressure ka effect badh sakta hai. AARC guidance adult aur pediatric endotracheal tubes mein catheter se lumen ka less than 50% occlusion recommend karti hai, neonatal limit alag hai. Age, tube internal size aur local validated sizing chart follow karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Airway ko completely block karne wala catheter airflow compromise kar sakta hai.
- **B (Galat):** Bed number patient ya tube ke anatomical size ka indicator nahi hai.
- **C (Sahi):** Tube lumen ke relative correct catheter sizing gas passage aur suction safety support karti hai.
- **D (Galat):** Largest available catheter har tube mein suitable nahi hai. Excessive occlusion harm kar sakti hai.

**Exam clue:** Catheter size depends on airway lumen, age and protocol.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://doi.org/10.4187/respcare.09548) · [Reference 2](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK593189/)

**Supplementary practice lead:** [Aarogyam Infinity FON MCQ Series Part 18](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m1UM3dvxEv4). Indexed title and tags include tracheostomy and suctioning. Direct retrieval failed. Specific coverage not verified.

### Q14. A conscious patient with an intact gag reflex needs airway support. Which device is generally inappropriate without special indications?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Clinically indicated suction of visible secretions
- **B.** Oropharyngeal airway
- **C.** Supplemental oxygen by suitable device
- **D.** Positioning to maintain airway patency

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Oropharyngeal airway**

Oropharyngeal airway ya OPA mouth se pharynx tak airway patency support karne wala adjunct hai. Intact gag reflex wale conscious patient mein OPA posterior throat ko stimulate karke gagging, vomiting aur aspiration ka risk la sakti hai. Device selection trained airway assessment, consciousness aur protective reflexes par depend karti hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Visible secretions ki clinically indicated suction patient assessment aur appropriate technique ke saath possible hai.
- **B (Sahi):** Intact gag reflex ke saath OPA generally inappropriate hai kyunki patient ise tolerate nahi kar sakta.
- **C (Galat):** Suitable supplemental oxygen device nasal ya mouth passage mein rigid OPA insert kiye bina oxygenation support kar sakti hai.
- **D (Galat):** Safe positioning airway patency maintain karne mein help kar sakti hai. Trauma restrictions consider karni chahiye.

**Exam clue:** OPA usually for unresponsive patients without gag reflex.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/critical-care-medicine/respiratory-arrest/airway-establishment-and-control?qt=Airway) · [Reference 2](https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/critical-care-medicine/how-to-do-basic-airway-procedures/how-to-insert-a-nasopharyngeal-airway?media=full)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

### Q15. A patient with a suspected basal skull fracture requires airway assessment. Which adjunct should not be inserted blindly through the nose?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Nasopharyngeal airway
- **B.** A properly applied external oxygen mask
- **C.** A pulse oximeter
- **D.** A stethoscope

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Nasopharyngeal airway**

Basal skull fracture mein skull ke base ki bone injured ho sakti hai. Nasopharyngeal airway ya NPA nose ke through pharynx tak jaati hai. Suspected skull-base injury, especially cribriform plate involvement, mein blind nasal instrumentation rare lekin serious harm ka risk rakhti hai. Trained emergency airway team safe alternative choose karti hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Sahi):** NPA nose mein insert hoti hai. Suspected skull-base fracture mein blind insertion avoid karna chahiye.
- **B (Galat):** External oxygen mask face ke bahar apply hoti hai aur skull base ke through instrument pass nahi karti.
- **C (Galat):** Pulse oximeter peripheral saturation estimate karne ke liye external sensor hai.
- **D (Galat):** Stethoscope breath sounds assess karne ke liye external device hai. Yeh nasal instrument nahi hai.

**Exam clue:** Suspected basilar skull fracture: avoid blind NPA insertion.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/critical-care-medicine/how-to-do-basic-airway-procedures/how-to-insert-a-nasopharyngeal-airway?media=full) · [Reference 2](https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/critical-care-medicine/respiratory-arrest/airway-establishment-and-control?qt=Airway)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q16. Which action helps maintain oxygen-cylinder safety during transport?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Carry it unsecured on the patient's lap
- **B.** Allow it to roll freely on the trolley
- **C.** Apply oil to the valve connections
- **D.** Secure the cylinder in an approved holder and protect it from impact

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Secure the cylinder in an approved holder and protect it from impact**

Medical oxygen cylinder high-pressure gas contain karti hai. Agar cylinder gir jaaye ya valve damage ho toh serious mechanical hazard ho sakta hai. Oxygen khud fuel nahi hai lekin combustion ko support karti hai. Isliye approved secure carrier, impact protection aur oil-free compatible equipment use karo. Patient transfer se pehle adequate oxygen supply aur equipment function check karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Unsecured cylinder lap se gir sakti hai aur patient ya staff ko injure kar sakti hai.
- **B (Galat):** Cylinder ko trolley par freely roll karne se impact aur valve damage ka risk badhta hai.
- **C (Galat):** Oil ya grease oxygen-rich environment mein ignition risk badha sakte hain. Oxygen fittings par unauthorized lubricant mat lagao.
- **D (Sahi):** Approved holder cylinder movement aur impact risk reduce karta hai.

**Exam clue:** Secure cylinder, protect valve and keep oil or grease away.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://www.who.int/publications/m/item/oxygen-cylinder-safety) · [Reference 2](https://www.england.nhs.uk/publication/national-patient-safety-alert-use-of-oxygen-cylinders-where-patients-do-not-have-access-to-medical-gas-pipeline-systems/)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q17. Why should oxygen delivery tubing be checked during a patient's transfer?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Tubing has no influence on oxygen delivery
- **B.** Every transfer automatically increases oxygen flow
- **C.** Oxygen can continue indefinitely without a source
- **D.** Kinks, disconnections or empty supply can interrupt oxygen delivery

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Kinks, disconnections or empty supply can interrupt oxygen delivery**

Transfer ke dauran oxygen tubing pull, kink ya disconnect ho sakti hai. Portable source ka supply limited ho sakta hai. Nurse adequate remaining supply, correct flow setting, tubing connection aur patient response check karti hai. Unstable patient ke liye appropriate escort aur emergency plan chahiye.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Kinked ya disconnected tubing oxygen flow interrupt kar sakti hai. Isliye tubing ka function important hai.
- **B (Galat):** Transfer apne aap oxygen flow increase nahi karta. Device setting prescribed requirement se match honi chahiye.
- **C (Galat):** Oxygen source finite ho sakta hai aur interruption ke baad therapy continue nahi hoti.
- **D (Sahi):** Kinks, disconnections aur depleted cylinder preventable delivery failures hain. Transfer mein inko check karna appropriate hai.

**Exam clue:** Before and during transfer: supply, flow, connection and response.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://www.england.nhs.uk/publication/national-patient-safety-alert-use-of-oxygen-cylinders-where-patients-do-not-have-access-to-medical-gas-pipeline-systems/) · [Reference 2](https://openstax.org/books/clinical-nursing-skills/pages/18-4-management-of-impaired-cardiopulmonary-functioning)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q18. Which action is appropriate before applying a prescribed oxygen mask?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Choose a device solely by color
- **B.** Cover the mask's required air-entrainment openings
- **C.** Explain its purpose, assess baseline respiratory status and verify the correct device
- **D.** Skip assessment because oxygen is always harmless

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Explain its purpose, assess baseline respiratory status and verify the correct device**

Oxygen ek treatment hai jiska device, flow aur target patient ki clinical requirement ke according choose hota hai. Baseline respiratory rate, effort, saturation aur mental status record karne se baad ka response compare ho sakta hai. Patient ko mask ka purpose explain karo, correct fit aur adapter verify karo aur required openings open rakho. Emergency mein assessment aur oxygen support ko unnecessary delay mat karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Color coding manufacturer-specific ho sakti hai. Sirf color dekh kar correct oxygen device ya concentration confirm nahi hoti.
- **B (Galat):** Air-entrainment openings block karne se Venturi mixture aur delivered concentration change ho sakti hai.
- **C (Sahi):** Explanation, baseline assessment aur correct device verification safe administration ke important steps hain.
- **D (Galat):** Oxygen useful hai lekin inappropriate dose ya device se harm ho sakta hai. Assessment zaroori hai.

**Exam clue:** Explain, assess, verify device and reassess.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://openstax.org/books/clinical-nursing-skills/pages/18-4-management-of-impaired-cardiopulmonary-functioning) · [Reference 2](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK596733/)

**Supplementary practice lead:** [Oxygen Therapy FON MCQ Countdown Series](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GRozFrA3VCg). Indexed title only, direct retrieval failed and specific coverage unverified. Not counted as verified dedicated mapping.

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q19. A patient has a tracheostomy and suddenly develops severe respiratory distress. Which approach is appropriate?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Seal all airway openings without assessment
- **B.** Activate emergency help and follow the tracheostomy airway emergency algorithm
- **C.** Blindly push equipment deep into the tube with force
- **D.** Assume distress is anxiety and wait

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Activate emergency help and follow the tracheostomy airway emergency algorithm**

Tracheostomy neck ke stoma se trachea mein airway access deti hai. Severe distress tube blockage, displacement ya doosre airway problem se ho sakti hai. Emergency team ko call karo aur patient-specific tracheostomy emergency algorithm follow karo. Oxygenation priority hai aur upper airway patent hai ya patient total laryngectomy ke baad hai, is distinction se support ka route decide hota hai. Blind force ya untrained tube replacement avoid karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Sab airway openings seal karne se available airflow band ho sakta hai. Airway anatomy assess karni chahiye.
- **B (Sahi):** Urgent help aur established tracheostomy algorithm systematic airway evaluation aur oxygenation support karte hain.
- **C (Galat):** Blind force se tissue injury, false passage ya tube displacement worsen ho sakta hai.
- **D (Galat):** Sudden severe respiratory distress ko anxiety assume karna life-threatening obstruction miss kar sakta hai.

**Exam clue:** Tracheostomy emergency: call for help and follow patient-specific airway algorithm.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://tracheostomy.org.uk/healthcare-staff/emergency-care/emergency-algorithm-tracheostomy) · [Reference 2](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK593189/)

**Supplementary practice lead:** [Aarogyam Infinity FON MCQ Series Part 18](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m1UM3dvxEv4). Indexed title and tags include tracheostomy and suctioning. Direct retrieval failed. Specific coverage not verified.

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q20. Which finding should be documented after an oxygen therapy adjustment?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Device, flow or concentration, saturation, respiratory status and response
- **B.** Only the wall outlet color
- **C.** Only the nurse's name without clinical findings
- **D.** No documentation if saturation improved

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Device, flow or concentration, saturation, respiratory status and response**

Oxygen therapy adjustment ke baad documentation se team ko pata chalta hai ki treatment kis device aur setting par diya gaya aur patient ka response kya tha. SpO2, respiratory rate, work of breathing, clinical symptoms, prescribed target aur time of change relevant hain. Zarurat par escalation aur clinician communication bhi record karo. Record ke saath ongoing reassessment continue hoti hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Sahi):** Wall outlet ka color delivered dose ya patient response establish nahi karta.
- **B (Galat):** Nurse ka naam accountability ka part ho sakta hai, lekin clinical observations replace nahi karta.
- **C (Galat):** Saturation improve ho tab bhi setting aur response document karna continuity of care ke liye important hai.
- **D (Galat):** Device, flow ya concentration, saturation aur respiratory status record karne se treatment effectiveness aur handover support hota hai.

**Exam clue:** Document the dose/device, target, patient response and time.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://openstax.org/books/clinical-nursing-skills/pages/18-4-management-of-impaired-cardiopulmonary-functioning) · [Reference 2](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34728574/)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.
